en.name: Nori (toasted seaweed sheets)
en.summary: Nori keeps 3–6 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard, and 1–2 years frozen in an unopened pack. The short cupboard figure is about crispness and aroma rather than safety — nori goes limp long before it becomes unsafe.
en.pantry: Sealed tight, away from heat, sunlight and damp, 3–6 months. That is shorter than for kombu or wakame and deliberately so: nori is a paper-thin sheet with an enormous surface area, and it loses its crispness and its sea aroma faster than any other dried seaweed. Keep the desiccant sachet in the bag, squeeze the air out and reseal after every single use — an hour open on a humid day is enough to take the snap out of a sheet. A limp sheet is not spoiled; pass it briefly over a low flame or a dry pan and it crisps up again.
en.fridge: The fridge is a poor home for nori. It is humid, the pack is opened and closed repeatedly, and every trip in and out invites condensation onto sheets whose whole appeal is dryness. If the only cool place you have is the fridge, at least seal the pack inside a second airtight bag and let it come fully back to room temperature before opening. Otherwise the cupboard, sealed and dark, is the better choice.
en.freezer: Unopened packs freeze well and keep 1–2 years at −18 °C (0 °F); this is the standard way to hold a bulk purchase. The rule that matters is on the way out: let the sealed pack come all the way back to room temperature before you open it, or moisture will condense straight onto the sheets and ruin them in minutes. Freeze the pack unopened, and do not put a half-used bag back in.
en.thawing: Let the sealed pack stand at room temperature until it is no longer cold to the touch, then open it. Never open a pack straight from the freezer.
spoilage: A stale, fishy or musty smell instead of a clean marine one.
Sheets that have gone soft and leathery and will not crisp up over heat.
Reddish or purple-brown patches, or a bleached, faded colour.
Visible mould or a sour smell in a pack that has taken up damp.
tips: Keep the desiccant sachet in the bag and reseal immediately after use.
Buy small packs rather than a big one you will keep opening.
Revive limp sheets over a low flame or in a dry pan.
Freeze whole unopened packs; let them warm fully before opening.

faq.a: 3–6 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard, or 1–2 years frozen in an unopened pack at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, unopened packs freeze well for 1–2 years. Let the pack return fully to room temperature before opening, or condensation will ruin the sheets.

faq.q: Is limp nori still safe to eat?
faq.a: Yes. Limpness is moisture, not spoilage. Crisp it over a low flame. Mould, a sour smell or a strong fishy smell mean it goes.

zh.name: 海苔
zh.summary: 海苔密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 3～6 個月；未開封整包冷凍則可放 1～2 年。櫥櫃期限之所以偏短，關鍵在脆度與香氣而不是安全——海苔在變得不安全之前，早就先軟掉了。
zh.pantry: 確實密封，避開高溫、陽光與潮濕，約 3～6 個月。這比昆布、裙帶菜短，而且是刻意的：海苔薄得像紙、表面積極大，脆度和海味流失的速度比任何一種乾燥海藻都快。乾燥劑留在袋子裡，每一次用完都把空氣擠掉、重新封好——潮濕的日子裡開著一小時，就足以讓一張海苔失去那個「喀」的聲音。軟掉的海苔不是壞掉：在小火上或乾鍋裡輕輕過一下，就會再脆起來。
zh.fridge: 冰箱對海苔而言不是好地方。它潮濕，包裝又會被反覆開關，每一次進出都在邀請水氣凝到這種「以乾為命」的薄片上。如果家裡唯一涼爽的地方只有冰箱，至少要把整包再裝進第二層密封袋，而且拿出來要完全回到室溫才打開。否則密封、避光的櫥櫃才是更好的選擇。
zh.freezer: 未開封的整包很適合冷凍，−18 °C 下可放 1～2 年，這也是囤貨的標準做法。真正關鍵的規則在拿出來的時候：一定要讓整包回到室溫再拆封，否則水氣會直接凝在海苔上，幾分鐘就毀掉一包。請整包未開封冷凍，用了一半的袋子就不要再冰回去。
zh.thawing: 讓密封的整包在室溫放到摸起來不再冰涼，再拆開。絕對不要把剛從冷凍拿出來的袋子直接打開。
spoilage: 聞起來有陳味、腥味或霉味，而不是乾淨的海味。
海苔變軟變韌，過火也脆不回來。
出現紅褐色或紫褐色斑塊，或顏色明顯褪白。
受潮的包裝裡看得到霉或聞到酸味。
tips: 乾燥劑留在袋內，用完立刻封回去。
買小包，不要買一大包反覆開合。
軟掉的海苔用小火或乾鍋過一下就能復活。
整包未開封冷凍，拿出來務必完全回溫再拆。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼暗處約 3～6 個月；未開封整包放 −18 °C 冷凍則是 1～2 年。
可以，未開封整包冷凍 1～2 年。拿出來一定要完全回到室溫再拆，否則結露會毀掉整包。
能。軟掉只是吸了水氣，不是壞掉，用小火烘一下就好。長霉、發酸或強烈腥味才要丟。
